The second part of the standard defines the transfer methods and application programming interface (API) for communicating learner records between services that adhere to the specification. This includes the format of requests and the expected responses. The Learner API enables privacy and security of learner data as it is transmitted between connected systems through formal information exchange agreements (e.g., Interservice Connection Agreement). The Learner API follows the guidelines of the Representational State Transfer (REST) software architecture style and is transferred via HTTP requests and responses.

The Internet Engineering Task Force is the premier Internet standards organization: an open global community that develops technical documents and standards for the Internet.
The IETF follows open and well-documented processes for setting standards, and published standards are made freely available.
Daily work happens through community participation, working groups, mailing lists, Internet-Drafts, RFCs, meetings, hackathons, and the IETF Datatracker.
Internet Engineering Steering Group - manages the standards process and technical work.
Internet Architecture Board - architectural oversight and liaison role.
Internet Research Task Force - related research groups.
RFC Editor - publication function for RFCs.
IETF Trust - holds IETF-related intellectual property and marks.
